items.title: My first open-source merge started with an ordinary evening
items.pt:
I didn’t plan to become an open-source contributor.
In January 2026, I didn’t really know what to do with my evening.
So I opened Apache Grails, found a small issue, tried a PR… and went to sleep.
Next thing I know, my phone lights up. Merged.

items.title: Good Engineers Have Opinions
items.pt:
One trait I have started noticing in good engineers, regardless of seniority, is that they are opinionated.

Not argumentative for the sake of it. Not the person who turns every code review into a hostage situation because someone used a different library. I mean they have a point of view. They have thought about the tradeoffs, they can say what they think we should do, and they are willing to stand behind it.

That matters more than I used to think.

items.title: Why Template Upwork Proposals Get Ignored (Rewrite One in 120 Words)
items.pt:
Most ignored Upwork proposals are not “bad English.” They are portable. The first screen could sit under any job title, for any client, in any industry, and busy US buyers can feel that in a few seconds.

Marketplace incentives push volume: save a master letter, swap the title, send. Client incentives push the opposite. They skim for one signal: this person read my brief and can start without drama.

items.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
items.pt: Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. items.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
items.pt: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. items.title: Dog-Breed Text-to-image Flow Matching from Pretraining to Fine-Tuning on 4 Consumer GPUs
items.pt: We generally perceive that training text-to-image diffusion models requires heavy compute: it is true if we aim at a comprehensive frontier model. This understanding prevents people from training their own models when getting started in the field. We develop MiniDog, a framework that enables pretraining diffusion transformers in 55 minutes and fine-tuning in another 15 minutes on four 3090 GPUs. For data, we use 26k dog images from ImageNet and caption them for pretraining and use 2k images gene

items.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
items.pt: How should demonstration quality be used during vision-language-action (VLA) pretraining to improve performance after target-task fine-tuning? We compare weighting, filtering, and conditioning across reward definitions and label granularities using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks. Within each VLA, we match demonstrations and training budgets. Additional comparisons examine pretraining data size and the roles of quality tags during fine-tuning and inference. Ac
